## Not covered by this file

Detection reads files. It cannot know the following, and neither can an agent until someone writes it down:

- Which conventions are enforced in review but not by a linter
- Which parts of the codebase are fragile, deprecated, or off limits
- What the definition of done is for this project
- Which commands are safe to run against production data
- Domain vocabulary that a newcomer would misread

Add those by hand. Keep them short and specific: an instruction an agent cannot follow is worse than no instruction, because it looks like guidance and costs a turn to disprove.

## Conventions not covered by the linter

- A rule id (`AG001`) is a public identifier. Never renumber or reuse one; add a
  new id instead. People put these in CI allowlists and suppression comments.
- Severity is a design decision, not an accident. `error` means the file will
  mislead an agent and needs a concrete justification. If a rule is based on a
  heuristic, it must be a `warning`.
- Every rule needs two tests: one input that fires it and one that must stay
  quiet. A rule with only a positive case has not been shown to avoid false
  positives.
- Two parsers exist in sibling projects for this ecosystem. Where this repository
  has an equivalence test, keep it; it is what catches silent divergence.

## Definition of done

A change is done when `pytest` passes and `agentsmd verify .` reports no errors on
this repository's own `AGENTS.md`. The second check is the one that matters: this
repository eats its own cooking, so a regression in detection shows up as a
finding against itself.

## Domain vocabulary

- **Detection** reads files and returns facts or `None`. It never returns a
  plausible default.
- **Verification** compares an existing document against detection results. It is
  the product; generation is the convenience.
- **`unavailable` versus `missing`** in `src/agentsmd/verify.py` is a distinction
  about the machine, not the document. A tool that is not installed here is
  `unavailable`; a tool that should exist and does not is `missing`. Conflating
  them produces false accusations.

## Fragile areas

- `detect_generated` is the most heuristic function here. It deliberately errs
  toward missing a generated file rather than flagging a hand-written one,
  because a false "do not edit" is worse than a missing warning.
- `src/agentsmd/verify.py` classifies missing tools per command rather than per
  ecosystem. Having a Node package manager installed says nothing about whether
  another one is, and the code must not pretend otherwise.
